source.title: MetaSAEs: Joint Training with a Decomposability Penalty Produces More Atomic Sparse Autoencoder Latents

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether feature atomicity in language-model SAE dictionaries changes using a new joint-training intervention and co-occurrence and fuzzing measures. It does not reproduce the toy-network method or directly test the toy-model superposition claim.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition and cites earlier results, but those are not results of this study. It reports a hyperparameter grid, a zero-penalty control, atomicity-related metrics, and qualitative feature splits. Reconstruction and cross-entropy costs are not catalogued as claim results. The Gemma co-occurrence scan is described as small and mixed, without configuration-specific numerical values.
record.test_reason: A methods paper. It proposes joint primary/meta SAE training with a decomposability penalty and reports only how that method compares with a solo SAE: change in mean |φ|, fuzzing, L2/CE and hand-picked feature splits. It uses SAEs and the superposition framing as tools. It does not measure whether LLM features are spread across neurons, whether SAEs recover sparse features, or whether SAE features are canonical units. It has no toy models, no capacity analysis and no 1-D versus multi-D comparison. The solo-SAE blending finding could loosely bear on V5, but it is shown only as a method-versus-baseline contrast, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors add that the CE overhead is modest (+0.6 pp over the solo SAE on GPT-2 large) and that the λ2=0 control attributes the gains to the penalty. They present the Gemma results as directional, from non-converged SAEs and an underpowered scan.
record.recipe_differences: The cited original concerns toy superposition models. This study jointly trains primary and meta SAEs on language-model activations and evaluates SAE feature co-occurrence and fuzzing, rather than testing toy-network feature geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with λ2 and σ2: the selected GPT-2 configuration improves the reported measures, while λ2 = 1.0 increases mean |φ|. Gemma co-occurrence results are mixed across its grid. The study evaluates one layer per model.

fits_no_version.finding: Solo SAE latents on GPT-2 large and Gemma 2 9B merge distinct word senses ('too', 'let', 'cookies', 'flash'). A different training objective splits these into separate latents, and the decomposition shifts with λ2/σ2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SAE latent inventory depends on the training objective (here a decomposability penalty), so solo-SAE latents are not canonical or atomic units. This bears loosely on V5, but it is shown only via own-method comparison and cherry-picked examples.

record.problems: Only one layer is evaluated per model. Gemma SAEs are described as not fully converged and its co-occurrence scan as underpowered, with wide confidence intervals. Meta-dictionary size is not ablated. Fuzzing is an automated interpretability measure rather than ground-truth feature recovery.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V4 links is overturned. Every row is the study's own method compared with a solo SAE baseline, i.e. T4. Selection is circular: the configuration was chosen on the same |φ| scan it is reported on. The case studies are hand-picked splitting candidates using cross-SAE |φ|. No verdicts are given because no version is tested; the original source (Toy Models) is only cited.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse-feature overload relative to dimensions, and the predicted regular geometry or sparsity-dependent transition are not tested.
Does not test whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while less important features share limited capacity, or whether that mechanism explains neuron polysemanticity.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Tests SAE-latent atomicity in two language models, not features spread across many neurons or SAE recovery against known ground-truth features.
Does not assess whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses decoder columns as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 large selected configuration and reported qualitative splits; Gemma 2 9B selected configuration and qualitative splits
reader_labels.reason: The selected GPT-2 setting reduces mean |φ| and improves fuzzing, and the case studies report distinct SAE features for separate senses; Gemma gives a positive fuzzing result and similar qualitative splits (r5, r11, r14-r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 large high-penalty settings and Gemma co-occurrence grid
reader_labels.reason: The co-occurrence effect is not uniform: all λ2 = 1.0 GPT-2 settings increase |φ|, and Gemma co-occurrence results are described as small and mixed (r7-r9, r12-r13).
